eyes-of-wakanda: An animated anthology about Wakandan warriors on missions across the centuries, starting in ancient times. Nothing else on the list is set this early, so it goes first; the films don't depend on it.
marvel-one-shot-agent-carter: A 15-minute short set in 1946, a year after The First Avenger, with Peggy Carter at the SSR. Side story; the main sequence doesn't depend on it.
captain-marvel: Released in 2019 but set in the 1990s, with a younger Nick Fury long before the Avengers. It also introduces the Skrulls, who come back in Secret Invasion and The Marvels.
iron-man: Back to the present day. This 2008 film is where the MCU started, and Tony Stark builds his first suit here.
iron-man-2: Picks up a few months after Iron Man and overlaps with the same week as The Incredible Hulk and Thor. Natasha Romanoff shows up for the first time here.
marvel-one-shot-a-funny-thing-happened-o: A 4-minute short with Coulson on his way to New Mexico, which is why it sits right before Thor. Side story; the main sequence doesn't depend on it.
marvel-one-shot-the-consultant: A short with Coulson and Sitwell dealing with a loose end from The Incredible Hulk, set just before The Avengers. Side story; nothing later depends on it.
marvel-one-shot-item-47: A short set after the Battle of New York, about a couple who find a leftover alien gun. Side story; the main sequence doesn't depend on it.
thor-the-dark-world: Set about a year after the Battle of New York. Marvel's own timeline puts it before Iron Man 3, so that's the order here. The Aether introduced here comes back later.
marvel-one-shot-all-hail-the-king: Follows up a character from Iron Man 3, so it comes right after it. It also starts a thread about the Ten Rings that Shang-Chi picks up years later.
guardians-of-the-galaxy: We leave Earth entirely. Set in 2014, the same year as The Winter Soldier, and it's where Peter Quill and the Guardians first come together.
guardians-of-the-galaxy-vol-2: Set only a few months after the first Guardians, so we stay in space and watch them back to back.
i-am-groot-t1: Baby Groot shorts, a few minutes each. Marvel's timeline puts both seasons right after Vol. 2, while we're still with the Guardians. Nothing later depends on them.
daredevil-netflix-t1: Set in Hell's Kitchen in the years after the Battle of New York. It introduces Wilson Fisk, who returns in Daredevil: Born Again.
jessica-jones-t1: A private investigator in Hell's Kitchen, around the same time as Daredevil. Luke Cage is introduced here before he gets his own series.
ant-man: Set right after Age of Ultron, with Scott Lang taking over Hank Pym's suit. Scott joins the bigger picture in Civil War.
daredevil-t2: Brings in Frank Castle and Elektra, who carry into The Punisher and The Defenders.
luke-cage-t1: Luke Cage moves from Jessica Jones to Harlem and gets his own series. One of the four shows that lead into The Defenders.
iron-fist-t1: Introduces Danny Rand, the last of the four heroes who team up in The Defenders.
the-defenders: Daredevil, Jessica Jones, Luke Cage and Iron Fist team up, so it comes after all four of their introductions.
black-widow: Released in 2021, but set right after Civil War with Natasha on the run, so I put it here. It also introduces Yelena Belova, who has a big role in Thunderbolts*.
black-panther: Set about a week after Civil War, with T'Challa going home to take the throne of Wakanda.
the-punisher-t1: Frank Castle's own series, following his debut in Daredevil Season 2.
doctor-strange: Stephen Strange's origin brings magic into the MCU. His training covers a long stretch with no firm dates, so I put it here, before the run-up to Infinity War.
jessica-jones-t2: Set after The Defenders, and it digs into how Jessica got her powers.
luke-cage-t2: Back in Harlem after The Defenders, with a new rival, Bushmaster.
iron-fist-t2: Set after The Defenders, with Danny looking after the city in Matt Murdock's absence.
daredevil-t3: Picks up after The Defenders, with Fisk back in the picture. It's the Netflix season Daredevil: Born Again builds on most.
thor-ragnarok: Thor and Hulk end up on Sakaar, which explains where Hulk went after Age of Ultron. Its final scene leads straight into Infinity War.
jessica-jones-t3: The last Netflix Marvel season released, and it closes out Jessica's arc. Nothing in the films depends on it.
ant-man-and-the-wasp: Scott is under house arrest after Civil War, and the Quantum Realm becomes part of the plot. That Quantum Realm matters again soon.
loki-t1: Starts from a moment in Endgame and introduces the TVA, the agency that polices timelines. This is where the multiverse becomes the main thread for the next phase.
what-if-t1: Animated alternate takes on MCU moments, like Peggy Carter taking the super-soldier serum. Mostly standalone; it sits after Loki because that's where the multiverse opens up.
marvel-zombies: A four-episode animated series set in the zombie world from What If...? Season 1, so it comes right after it.
wandavision: Wanda in a sitcom-perfect town after Endgame. It leads into Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness and Agatha All Along.
shang-chi-and-the-legend-of-the-ten-ring: Shang-Chi's origin, set in the year after Endgame. It explains the Ten Rings organization that's been around since the first Iron Man.
the-falcon-and-the-winter-soldier: Sam and Bucky after Endgame, and the question of who should carry the shield. It leads directly into Captain America: Brave New World and Thunderbolts*.
spider-man-far-from-home: Peter's school trip to Europe after Endgame. No Way Home picks up right after its ending, but we take a detour through the older Spider-Man films first, on purpose.
eternals: Set after Endgame. It's the last MCU stop before the Spider-Man detour, which starts with the next title and runs back to 2002.
spider-man-2002-sam-raimi: Yes, we're going back to 2002. Trust me, there's a reason: this is a different Peter Parker from a different universe, and you'll want these films fresh before No Way Home.
the-amazing-spider-man-2012: A reboot with Andrew Garfield as Peter Parker, in yet another universe. Same origin, new cast, plus Gwen Stacy and the Lizard.
the-amazing-spider-man-2-2014: Andrew Garfield's second and last solo film, with Electro and Harry Osborn. It's the final piece you need before No Way Home.
venom-2018: Tom Hardy's Eddie Brock in Sony's own corner of the multiverse, with no Spider-Man in it. It's in this block because the Venom films cross paths with the multiverse around No Way Home.
venom-let-there-be-carnage-2021: Eddie and Venom against Carnage. It sits right before No Way Home for a reason we won't spoil.
spider-man-no-way-home: Back to the MCU, picking up right after Far From Home. This is why the Raimi and Webb films came first.
venom-the-last-dance-2024: Tom Hardy's last Venom film. It picks up where No Way Home left Eddie, so it has to come after it.
spider-man-into-the-spider-verse: Animated, with Miles Morales in his own universe. It's optional because it doesn't connect to the MCU; it sits here with the other Spider-Man films.
spider-man-across-the-spider-verse: Miles's second film, ending on a cliffhanger whose conclusion isn't out yet. Optional for the MCU; it continues straight from Into the Spider-Verse.
doctor-strange-in-the-multiverse-of-madn: Strange deals with the fallout of No Way Home and meets America Chavez, who can jump between universes. It leans heavily on WandaVision.
hawkeye: Set at Christmas after Endgame, and it follows on from the Black Widow post-credits scene. Maya Lopez debuts here before her own series, Echo, a few titles later.
black-panther-wakanda-forever: Riri Williams debuts here, so it has to come before Ironheart, which picks up with her back home in Chicago.
echo: Maya Lopez after Hawkeye, back home in Oklahoma with her family. It's a bridge into Daredevil: Born Again.
she-hulk-attorney-at-law: Jennifer Walters is Bruce Banner's cousin and gets her powers from him, so the Hulk films should come first. Matt Murdock also turns up, ahead of Daredevil: Born Again.
ms-marvel: Kamala Khan, a teen Captain Marvel fan from Jersey City, gets powers of her own. Watch it before The Marvels, which she's a big part of.
thor-love-and-thunder: Picks up with Thor still travelling with the Guardians after Endgame, and brings back Jane Foster, last seen in The Dark World.
ironheart: Riri Williams goes home to Chicago after Wakanda Forever and runs into the Hood.
werewolf-by-night: A black-and-white monster-hunter special, under an hour long. It doesn't connect to other titles yet, so it can go almost anywhere after Endgame.
the-guardians-of-the-galaxy-holiday-spec: A 40-minute Christmas special with Mantis and Drax looking for a gift for Quill. It's canon and sets up a couple of things Vol. 3 uses, so it comes before it, with Quantumania in between as on Marvel's timeline.
ant-man-and-the-wasp-quantumania: Marvel's timeline puts it between the Holiday Special and Guardians Vol. 3. Kang, a version of the character from Loki S1's finale, shows up here, and Loki S2 follows that thread.
guardians-of-the-galaxy-vol-3: Comes after the Holiday Special, which sets up a couple of things here. It closes out the Guardians lineup that started in 2014.
secret-invasion: Nick Fury and the Skrulls from Captain Marvel, years later. It continues Fury's arc into The Marvels.
the-marvels: Carol Danvers, Monica Rambeau from WandaVision and Kamala Khan from Ms. Marvel keep swapping places when they use their powers. That's why Ms. Marvel comes first.
loki-t2: Picks up right after Loki S1, but it's here because Marvel's timeline puts it after The Marvels, even though it came out a month earlier. A quick look at the S1 finale helps.
blade-1998: Released in 1998, a decade before Iron Man. I put the pre-MCU films here as one block, because Deadpool & Wolverine makes more sense with them fresh.
daredevil-2003-ben-affleck: Kept in release order with the other pre-MCU films, so Elektra, its spin-off, follows it. If you can, watch the director's cut: it restores a subplot the theatrical version dropped.
elektra-2005: A spin-off of Daredevil (2003) with Jennifer Garner, so it follows that film.
x-men-first-class: Set in 1962 around the Cuban Missile Crisis, with young Charles and Erik. From here the Fox X-Men films follow their own timeline instead of release order.
x-men-origins-wolverine: Logan's backstory, from the 1800s to the late '70s, so in story order it goes before X-Men (2000). The Deadpool films reference its version of Wade Wilson.
x-men-2000: Wolverine and Rogue arrive at Xavier's school in the first Fox X-Men film. It comes after Origins because it's set years later.
the-wolverine: Logan in Japan, after The Last Stand. A standalone Wolverine film.
x-men-days-of-future-past: Wolverine is sent back from a grim future to 1973, linking the original cast with the First Class one. It's the hinge of the whole Fox timeline.
x-men-apocalypse: The younger cast in 1983 against Apocalypse. It follows the timeline Days of Future Past changed.
dark-phoenix: The younger cast in 1992, with Jean Grey losing control of her powers. It closes the run that started with First Class; the Deadpool films and Logan come after it.
deadpool: Ryan Reynolds' mercenary in the Fox mutant world, with Colossus and Negasonic Teenage Warhead. Its timeline is loose, so it sits near the end of the Fox films.
the-new-mutants: Young mutants held in a hospital, played as a horror film. It picks up a thread from X-Men: Apocalypse's post-credits scene and shares footage with Logan, so it sits right before Logan.
logan: Set in 2029, the furthest-forward point of the Fox films, with an older Logan and Charles. It closes the Fox block before Deadpool & Wolverine.
deadpool-wolverine: Back to the MCU. The TVA pulls Deadpool out of the Fox world, which is why all those Fox films came first.
agatha-all-along: Agatha Harkness from WandaVision gathers a coven to walk the Witches' Road. You'll want WandaVision fresh in your head.
daredevil-born-again-t1: Matt Murdock and Wilson Fisk on a collision course, now with Fisk in politics. It continues the Netflix Daredevil seasons, so those come first.
captain-america-brave-new-world: Sam Wilson's first film as Captain America, with Thaddeus Ross now U.S. President. It pulls threads from The Incredible Hulk and The Falcon and the Winter Soldier.
thunderbolts: Yelena, Bucky, John Walker, Ghost and Red Guardian forced to work together. Each comes from an earlier film or series, mainly Black Widow and The Falcon and the Winter Soldier.
the-fantastic-four-first-steps: The Fantastic Four in their own retro-futuristic universe, separate from the MCU's Earth. It needs no prep from earlier titles; it's here because Marvel's timeline puts it after Thunderbolts*.
wonder-man: Marvel's timeline puts it after First Steps. Ben Kingsley's Trevor Slattery returns, so Iron Man 3, All Hail the King and Shang-Chi are the ones to have seen; otherwise it stands alone.
the-punisher-one-last-kill: A one-off special with Jon Bernthal's Frank Castle. Marvel's timeline puts it right after Daredevil: Born Again S2, and it came out a week after that season ended.
visionquest-t1: The last title on Marvel's own timeline. It finishes the story that WandaVision started and Agatha All Along continued, so both come first.
spider-man-brand-new-day: Tom Holland's next Spider-Man film after No Way Home. Marvel's Disney+ timeline doesn't list it yet, so it goes at the end; it builds directly on how No Way Home ends.
